LESSON: READING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Reading 2.1 Reading aloud (Articulation) (2 lessons) By the end of the sub-stran
Topic 2.6: Reading Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading Comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are reading texts important in learning a foreign language?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify appropriate expressions from reading texts
2. value the role of reading comprehension in learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING COMPREHENSION
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading Comprehension helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify appropriate expressions from reading texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify appropriate expressions from reading texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify appropriate expressions from reading texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify appropriate expressions from reading texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Value the role of reading comprehension in learning

What this means
In this part you learn to value the role of reading comprehension in learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the role of reading comprehension in learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Comprehension to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the role of reading comprehension in learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading Comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify appropriate expressions from reading texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Comprehension to a partner. (skill: value the role of reading comprehension in learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading Comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify appropriate expressions from reading texts.
3. Practise this skill: value the role of reading comprehension in learning.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading Comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading Comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading Comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are reading texts important in learning a foreign language?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading Comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify appropriate expressions from reading texts.
5. Be able to: value the role of reading comprehension in learning.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
